title: Option premium: intrinsic value, time value and moneyness
objectives: Split premium into intrinsic and time value.
body_md:
**Premium = intrinsic value + time value.**

- **Intrinsic value (call)** = max(S − K, 0); **(put)** = max(K − S, 0).
- **Time value** = premium − intrinsic value; it decays to zero at expiry.

## Moneyness

| State | Call | Put |
|---|---|---|
| **ITM** (in the money) | S > K | S < K |
| **ATM** (at the money) | S ≈ K | S ≈ K |
| **OTM** (out of the money) | S < K | S > K |

## What raises premium

| Factor | Call | Put |
|---|---|---|
| Spot price up | Up | Down |
| Strike higher | Down | Up |
| **Volatility up** | Up | Up |
| **Time to expiry longer** | Up | Up |
| Interest rate up | Up (slightly) | Down |
| Dividends expected | Down | Up |

Example: call K = 100, spot 108, premium 11: intrinsic 8, time value 3.

> **Exam tip:** OTM options have only time value.
example: Put K = 50, spot 46, premium 6.5. Intrinsic = 4, time value = 2.5. The put is in the money.
say: Time value decays every day; buyers fight the clock.
Higher volatility makes both calls and puts more expensive.
never: Time value rises as expiry nears.

check.why: A call is in the money when spot exceeds strike.
